companyDescription: Space launch + lunar lander · Alpha small-lift rocket, Blue Ghost lunar program, Elytra orbital vehicle — NASA CLPS + national security launch exposure
priceNote: ร่วงหนักจากระดับ offering $48 → $27.88 หลัง dilution overhang จาก secondary offering 12M shares; ยังไม่นับ Alpha Block 2 / Blue Ghost 2 catalysts ที่ยังไม่มาถึง
summary: Firefly just took a ~40% dilution-driven haircut from its $48 follow-on offering price down to ~$28, even as fundamentals improved (Q1 2026 revenue +45% YoY to $80.9M, beat on EPS) and Wall Street stayed bullish (avg target $45.75, Jefferies/KeyBanc at $50–52). Two dated catalysts — Alpha Block 2 debut (~Sep 30, 2026) and Blue Ghost Mission 2 (H2 2026) — sit ahead, but net losses (-$96.7M Q1) and continued share overhang keep this a high-beta speculative play, not a core holding.

catalysts.name: Alpha Block 2 debut (Flight 8 / VICTUS HAZE)
catalysts.description: First flight of the upgraded Alpha Block II rocket — longer airframe, stronger composites, in-house avionics. Targets national security responsive-launch demand (incl. Golden Dome).

catalysts.name: Blue Ghost Mission 2
catalysts.description: Second NASA CLPS lunar lander mission, now a dual-spacecraft (lander + Elytra Dark orbital vehicle) architecture; assembly/testing accelerating, launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 earnings
catalysts.description: Next quarterly print — market will watch cash burn trajectory, backlog growth, and 2026 revenue guidance ($420–450M) progress after Q1's wide net loss.

risks: Share overhang: 12M-share secondary offering (4M new + 8M sold by holders) at $48 still digesting — further insider/lockup selling could cap rallies
Heavy net losses ($96.7M Q1 2026) and rising opex; execution risk on scaling Alpha cadence + Blue Ghost 2
Launch-vehicle binary risk — any Alpha Block 2 test/launch failure historically triggers high-single-digit % sector drawdowns (see Rocket Lab Neutron precedent)
Valuation still rich on a sales-multiple basis after the run from $16 to $73.80 52-week high; sector sentiment also wobbling on SpaceX IPO chatter

estimateDates.note: First Block II launch, national security demand read

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed holding 3.50–3.75% for 4 straight meetings; next FOMC decision Jul 29, 2026 — no cut priced in, limits multiple expansion for unprofitable growth names
macroRisk.inflationNote: Inflation data has kept the Fed on hold; no near-term catalyst for lower discount rates
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Space/defense capex names like FLY are rate-sensitive (still cash-burning) but partly insulated by government (NASA/DoD) contract backlog vs. pure consumer-discretionary growth
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — no Fed catalyst either way before Alpha Block 2 launch; stock-specific dilution/execution risk matters far more than macro right now
